output.brief:
The rise in cancellations is mostly not a pricing problem. It comes from the Quillbook connector. Quillbook retired its old invoice interface on 30 March, and since then the connector has silently dropped or duplicated invoices. 58,300 invoices were affected across 1,212 accounts, and 34% of those accounts have cancelled, against 8% of Quillbook accounts with no failure. Churn for Quillbook accounts rose to about 6% a month whether or not they were repriced, and Founders accounts with the $39 price lock were hit equally. Accounts with no connector show almost no change, at about 1.9%, at any seat size. So the "bigger increase, more churn" pattern from finance only reflects that bigger accounts use Quillbook more. Tallymarsh changes are tiny and within normal variation.
Next steps: make the Quillbook v3 fix the top engineering priority. Contact every Quillbook account, including those that cancelled, to correct their invoices. Keep the duplicate-invoice hold on, because it protects customers' books. Do not roll back the price, and do not start the Tallymarsh rebuild yet. Review the Tallymarsh logs first. Also fix support response times for sync tickets. I'm fairly confident in this diagnosis.
